title: Mean Groundwater Velocity from Tracer Test

v.description: Mean linear velocity between injection and detection points

L.description: Straight-line distance from injection to detection

t_mean.description: Mean residence time (centroid of breakthrough curve)

applicability: In karst: velocity can be very high (10–1000+ m/day through conduits). In porous media: typically 0.01–10 m/day. In fractured rock: highly variable depending on fracture aperture and connectivity.

title: Tracer Recovery

R.description: Fraction of injected tracer mass recovered at detection point

C(t).description: Tracer concentration at detection point as function of time

applicability: Discrete sampling: R ≈ Σ[Ci × Qi × Δti] / M₀. Recovery < 100%: tracer lost to other flow paths, sorption, degradation, or matrix diffusion. Low recovery (< 50%) means incomplete understanding of flow system.

title: Longitudinal Dispersivity from Breakthrough Curve

σ².description: Spatial variance of the tracer cloud = (σ_t × v)²

applicability: Scale-dependent: α_L ≈ 0.1 × L (Gelhar relationship) as a rough estimate. Laboratory-scale: 0.01–0.1 m. Field-scale 10 m: α ≈ 0.1–1 m. Field-scale 1000 m: α ≈ 10–100 m.

title: Lugeon Value (from Packer Test)

Lu.description: Lugeon value (liters/min per meter of test interval at 1 MPa)

L_test.description: Length of test interval between packers

P_test.description: Effective test pressure at the interval

applicability: 1 Lugeon ≈ k = 1.3 × 10⁻⁷ m/s (approximate). Grouting targets: dam curtains typically grouted to < 3–5 Lu. Closure criterion < 3 Lu in final verification holes is common. Test conducted at multiple pressures (ascending/descending) to identify flow behavior (laminar, turbulent, dilation, washout).

title: GIN Method — Grouting Intensity Number

V.description: Volume of grout injected per meter of stage

applicability: Typical GIN values: 500–2500 bar·L/m for dam curtain grouting. Single stable mix (W:C = 0.67–1.0 with superplasticizer). Stop grouting when: P reaches P_max, V reaches V_max, or P×V reaches GIN limit — whichever comes first. Computer-monitored in real time.

title: Grout Cement Content by Weight
applicability: Traditional dam grouting: start at W:C = 5:1 (thin), thicken progressively to 3:1, 2:1, 1:1, 0.8:1, 0.6:1 based on grout take. GIN method: single stable mix at W:C = 0.67–1.0 with superplasticizer. For volume estimation: 1 bag (42.6 kg) cement at W:C = 1.0 yields ~58 L of grout.

title: Grout Penetration in Fracture (Bingham Fluid)
simplified_form: R_max ≈ (ΔP × w²) / (6 × τ₀)  (for Bingham flow in parallel plates)
applicability: Grout penetration is extremely sensitive to fracture aperture (w² dependence). Doubling aperture quadruples penetration. Cement grout cannot penetrate fractures < 0.1–0.2 mm; microfine cement needed for 0.05–0.1 mm; chemical grout for finer.

title: Compaction Grout Injection Pressure (Limiting)

P_max.description: Maximum injection pressure before hydraulic fracture or heave

σ'_v.description: Effective vertical stress at injection depth

c_u.description: Undrained shear strength of surrounding soil

applicability: Approximate — actual fracture pressure depends on in-situ stress state and soil strength. Monitor surface heave continuously during compaction grouting (typically limit to < 12 mm). Injection rate typically 15–75 L/min (4–20 gal/min).

title: Jet Grout Column Diameter (Empirical)
equation: D_col ≈ f(system, soil type, energy, withdrawal rate)
applicability: Typical ranges: Single-fluid system: 0.6–1.2 m. Double-fluid (grout+air): 1.0–1.8 m. Triple-fluid (water+air+grout): 1.5–2.5 m. Diameter varies with soil type (larger in soft clay than dense sand), nozzle pressure, rotation speed, and withdrawal rate. Always verify with trial columns.

title: Grout Curtain Effectiveness (Seepage Reduction)
equation: Q_grouted / Q_ungrouted ≈ k_grouted / k_original  (for curtain of thickness t)

Q.description: Seepage flow rate (per unit length of dam)

applicability: Simplified — assumes curtain is the controlling element. More rigorous: Q = k_grouted × H / t_curtain where H = head across curtain, t_curtain = curtain thickness. Multi-row curtain: effective thickness ≈ row spacing. Grouting reduces k by 1–3 orders of magnitude typically (e.g., from 5 Lu to < 1 Lu).
